record.paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Give a characterization of infine words whose complexity satisfies limn p(n)/n = 2.

evidence.quote: Give a characterization of infine words whose complexity satisfies limn p(n)/n = 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet and let x = x_1 x_2 x_3 ... be an infinite word over A. For each integer n ≥ 1, let p_x(n) denote the factor complexity of x, defined as the number of distinct factors (contiguous finite subwords) of x of length n.

Provide a characterization of all infinite words x over a finite alphabet whose factor complexity satisfies
   lim_{n → ∞} p_x(n) / n = 2.

The characterization should describe the structural, combinatorial, or dynamical properties (for example, in terms of substitutions, codings of rotations, S-adic representations, or other intrinsic descriptions) that are equivalent to this asymptotic complexity condition.
artifact.status_search_result: Sturmian words are characterized as the infinite words with minimal aperiodic complexity p(n)=n+1, but a complete structural characterization of infinite words satisfying lim p(n)/n = 2 does not appear in the standard literature. Recent surveys on low factor complexity discuss Tijdeman-type generalizations and S-adic representations of linearly recurrent words, but no source clearly states a definitive characterization for the precise asymptotic ratio 2. The status appears to remain unresolved, but this could not be verified conclusively.

status_evidence.title: Infinite Words with very Low Factor Complexity
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of infinite words with low factor complexity, focusing on Sturmian words (p(n)=n+1) and generalizations.
status_evidence.claim: No definitive characterization for words with lim p(n)/n = 2 is highlighted; the survey concentrates on minimal-complexity classes.

status_evidence.title: A characterization of words of linear complexity
status_evidence.snippet: Provides a characterization of words with p(n)=O(n) via concatenations of elements of a bounded-complexity set.
status_evidence.claim: Relates to linear-complexity words generally, not specifically to those with limit ratio equal to 2.
